title: U.S. House · Texas's 36th District
area: An East Texas district covering areas east and northeast of Houston, including Deer Park, Lumberton, and Woodville.

context.text: Rep. Brian Babin is the incumbent under Texas's 2026 congressional map. Rhonda Hart won the Democratic nomination.

candidates.name: Brian Babin
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative (since 2015); chair, House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology

summary.text: Brian Babin is the Republican incumbent for Texas's 36th District. A dentist from Woodville, he is an Air Force veteran who held local offices there, including mayor, before winning the seat in 2014 after a Republican primary runoff. He serves on the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee and has chaired the Science, Space, and Technology Committee since the start of the 119th Congress.

background.text: Born in Port Arthur, Texas, in 1948 and grew up in Beaumont; his House biography calls him a lifelong resident of East Texas.

Earned a B.S. in biology from Lamar University in 1973 and a D.D.S. from the University of Texas Dental Branch in Houston in 1976. His House biography says he worked as a merchant seaman, janitor, musician, disc jockey, and letter carrier to pay for school, and served as an airborne artilleryman in the Texas Army National Guard.
Served as a captain in the U.S. Air Force from 1975 to 1979 after dental school, stationed in Ramstein, Germany.
Returned to East Texas in 1979 and opened a dental practice in Woodville, which he ran for more than 30 years.

Held local office in Woodville as an alderman or city councilman, mayor, and school board member, and served as a Tyler County Chamber of Commerce director and vice president and as Lions Club president.

Has served on the Lower Neches Valley Authority since 1999 and has been a member of the Texas Historical Commission, the Texas State Board of Dental Examiners, and the Deep East Texas Council of Governments.
Won the 2014 Republican primary runoff against Ben Streusand on May 27, 2014, and the November 2014 general election. He was sworn in on January 5, 2015, succeeding Steve Stockman.

Serves on the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and has chaired the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology since the start of the 119th Congress. He previously chaired its Space and Aeronautics Subcommittee in 2023-2024 and was its ranking member in 2021-2022.
According to his House biography, he has been married to Roxanne since 1972, and they have five children and 17 grandchildren; he has served as a deacon at First Baptist Church of Woodville.

priorities.text: Chairs the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, which oversees NASA and federal research policy.

positions.summary: His official site says Congress must end "catch and release" and keep the promise to build the wall and enforce the border.
positions.quote: We must end “catch and release”, through which illegal border crossers, immediately upon setting foot on our soil, can make unjustified claims of persecution and be released into our nation.

positions.summary: His official site says he supports legislation letting concealed-carry permit holders carry from state to state.
positions.quote: I am actively supporting legislation to ensure that those with conceal carry permits are able to carry from state to state.

positions.summary: His official site says he promised to repeal the Affordable Care Act and replace it, and describes the House's 2017 American Health Care Act as a first step.
positions.quote: I promised the people of the 36th District of Texas that I would repeal Obamacare and replace it with a workable, affordable solution which lowers premiums while protecting those with preexisting conditions.

record.text: Chairs the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology in the 2025-2026 (119th) Congress, having previously chaired its Space and Aeronautics Subcommittee.
Also serves on the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure, including its Highways and Transit and Water Resources and Environment subcommittees.

summary.text: Rhonda Hart is the Democratic nominee for Texas's 36th District. She is a U.S. Army veteran and public policy advocate whose daughter, Kimberly Vaughan, was killed in the 2018 Santa Fe High School shooting, and she has since advocated for gun-storage laws. She ran for Texas's 14th District in 2024 and is running on gun safety, veterans' issues, and affordability.

background.text: Born in Nebraska; graduated from Wasilla High School in Alaska.

Served in the U.S. Army from 2000 to 2003 and earned an associate degree from the University of Alaska Southeast in 2009. She describes herself as a disabled veteran who receives her care through the VA.
Her daughter, Kimberly Vaughan, was one of ten people killed in the May 18, 2018, shooting at Santa Fe High School in Santa Fe, Texas.

After the shooting she became an advocate for stricter gun laws; in 2019 she attended the State of the Union address as a guest of Rep. Lizzie Fletcher and a House Judiciary Committee hearing on H.R. 8.
In her Candidate Connection survey, she says she has spent six years advocating for safer gun-storage laws and was an advocate for the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act of 2022 and Texas SB 435.
Won the Democratic nomination for Texas's 14th District in 2024 and lost the general election to Rep. Randy Weber. She won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary for the 36th District.

priorities.text: Advocates for stronger gun-storage laws, citing the loss of her daughter to gun violence.
priorities.quote: We all know that gun violence is preventable. That’s why I’ve spent the last six years fighting for safer gun storage laws, and it’s why I’ll keep fighting for common sense gun laws in Congress.

priorities.text: Supports improved veteran access to doctors, medical facilities, pensions, and long-term benefits.
Supports codifying Roe v. Wade into federal law.
priorities.quote: In Congress, I’ll fight to defend a woman’s right to choose and work to pass federal laws to codify Roe v. Wade.

positions.summary: Supports stricter gun-storage laws and says she helped pass the federal Bipartisan Safer Communities Act and a Texas gun-storage law.
positions.quote: I’ve spent the last six years fighting for safer gun storage laws

positions.summary: Supports federal legislation to codify Roe v. Wade and defend abortion access.
positions.quote: I believe that all women deserve the right to make their own healthcare decisions. In Congress, I’ll fight to defend a woman’s right to choose and work to pass federal laws to codify Roe v. Wade.

positions.summary: Lists ending tariffs among her campaign's key messages.
Lists raising the minimum wage among her campaign's key messages.
Lists taxing billionaires among her campaign's key messages.
Lists stopping deportations of construction workers among her campaign's key messages.
positions.quote: Stop deporting the workers who build the homes that people in this district need.
